storyline.arc: It began as an embedded terminal that could run Claude in a git worktree without wrecking your main checkout. It now runs on Windows, works in the background, reconstructs coding history you never tracked, and teaches you from it.

eras.blurb: The terminal learned to hold several sessions, speak both Claude and OpenCode, sandbox its worktrees, and summarize each commit from the interaction trace rather than the diff.
eras.title: Two backends, many sessions, and commits that explain themselves

eras.blurb: Sessions could now be exported, imported, attributed to a github id, and resumed across worktree modes, all under the name aGiTrack.
eras.title: Sharing sessions, counting sub-agent tokens, and a new name

eras.blurb: Native Windows support arrived with an MSI pipeline, alongside background git threads, idle backoff, and a pre-commit hook stopping agents from touching the base repo.
eras.title: Windows, MSI installers, and a guard against agents committing to base

eras.blurb: aGiTrack learned to watch quietly with a persistent watermark, and --backtrace let it rebuild coding history from repos that had never been tracked.
eras.title: Background mode and reconstructing history you never recorded

eras.blurb: AI-generated personalized lessons, static-exported dashboards, atomic writes, self-updating daemons, and a long hunt for the token counts that never quite matched.
eras.title: Learning from your own transcripts, on a dashboard that finally holds still

moments.detail: The want was simple to say and annoying to build: run two sessions on two different branches at once, without ever touching the base branch checked out in the repo directory. Before this, everything funneled into one shared merge target, so concurrent sessions kept landing in the same place and stomping each other. The fix made the merge branch a per-session property (with a picker at session creation, defaulting to the base branch), which promptly made the old --git-base-branch option look redundant, and the README got a whole branch-management section explaining the new rules.
moments.summary: Merge branches went per-session so concurrent work stopped colliding in the same place.

thoughts.note: Framing it as user choice rather than plumbing: default to the base branch, but let each session opt into another one.
thoughts.quote: I'd like to allow concurrent sessions on independent branches, without having to change the base branch in the repo directory. The user can select whether to apply merge changes to the base branch (default option) or to a different branch. When merging into a different branch than the one the repo's main directory is checked out, the status bar should emphasize that the branch the changes will be merged into is not the one on the directory. The emphasis may change if the user changes the branch on the repo directory.

thoughts.note: Noticing that once each session carries its own merge branch, the global base-branch flag has nothing left to do.
thoughts.quote: Perhaps the git-base-branch option is no longer needed now?
